Bone repair

Animal models often report greater new-bone formation, but findings vary. Small human distraction studies and a 2026 cleft-graft study report selected structural gains, while the vascular-light arm of that graft study did not improve bone-bridge outcomes.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Animal models often report greater new-bone formation, but findings vary. Small human distraction studies and a 2026 cleft-graft study report selected structural gains, while the vascular-light arm of that graft study did not improve bone-bridge outcomes.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Bone > Bone repair category contains 208 database records, representing 208 unique titles. It includes 191 animal records, 16 review or meta-analysis records, seven in-vitro records, and one unclassified title. Six additional human publications are narrowly mapped from related grafting and distraction categories; they are kept separate from the exact-category count. Several graft papers measure only postoperative symptoms, not structural repair.

Human and clinical evidence

The mapped human reports include a nine-person randomized mandibular-distraction study, a 20-person self-controlled distraction study, two randomized cleft-graft studies, one non-randomized controlled graft study, and one newer cleft-graft clinical report whose design is not clearly classified. The 2013 controlled and 2024 randomized graft reports measured short-term pain, edema, or temperature rather than structural bone formation (Cunha et al. 2013 Guerrini et al. 2024). The small 2015 randomized distraction study found higher radiographic bone density after low-level laser treatment, although the control group had a higher proportion of immature bone (Çakir-Özkan et al. 2015). The self-controlled study reported better bone quality during consolidation (Abd-Elaal et al. 2015). In 87 patients with cleft lip and palate, local PBM was associated with more favorable bone-bridge scores than control, whereas vascular PBM did not improve that outcome (Dos Santos et al. 2026). A 2025 vascular-PBM graft report found no between-group difference in facial pain or edema; these symptoms are not bone-healing measures (de Freitas et al. 2025). The 2025 and 2026 graft reports are from the same center, and participant overlap is not clear, so their sample sizes should not be added.

Animal evidence

The 191 animal records include 161 rat, 26 rabbit, three mouse, and one sheep study. Many test experimental defects, fractures, or graft materials. Reviews generally describe increased bone formation in some models, but results depend on model and material and do not establish patient benefit (Rosso et al. 2019).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

Seven records include cell experiments; six are reported alongside animal work and one is a standalone in-vitro study. No standalone ex-vivo study was identified in the exact category.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Reported protocols include 830-nm near-infrared laser at 40 mW and 8.4 J/cm² for eight sessions at 48-hour intervals in the distraction trial; 905-nm laser sessions during consolidation; and 880-nm near-infrared light at 100 mW and 4 J per point over 14 extraoral points in the local cleft-graft protocol. Vascular PBM used red light at the radial artery. Animal work varies widely in wavelength, dose, defect, and graft material.

Interpretation

The extensive preclinical literature supports biological effects in selected models, while human evidence is limited to specific oral reconstructive procedures. Symptom changes after graft surgery should not be mistaken for faster structural bone healing.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for selected short-term structural bone outcomes in small mapped human graft and distraction studies Very low for general bone union, function, and long-term durability across patients
Publications and records214 unique titles (214 database records; 208 exact-category titles plus 6 narrowly mapped human reports)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category is dominated by animal models and contains only a few mapped human reports with different procedures and outcomes. One small randomized distraction study, one self-controlled study, and a cleft-graft study report selected structural measures, while postoperative symptom reports are not evidence of bone repair. Replication with blinded imaging and longer follow-up is needed.
